objective: Determine a conservative, falsifiable evidence contract for RUNTIME_SUBJECT_INVARIANT: when may an already-bound higher-tier runtime subject remain representative after successor repository changes without composing historical runtime evidence into unsupported current-generation credit?
hypothesis: A runtime-subject manifest that binds declared inputs, observed runtime-relevant inputs, execution/config/environment identity, and a fail-closed change-impact rule can certify non-interference for some successor changes while preserving exact-source evidence boundaries.
counterhypothesis: Dynamic imports, configuration, data dependencies, environment-sensitive behavior, reflection, and undeclared inputs make such invariance certification unsound in practice; the safe rule is always invalidate/replay after any successor semantic change.
